text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert - Transit Gateway route propagation lag detected in us-west-2c (AZC). metric=TGW.RoutePropagationDelay > 30s across multiple route-tables. Pager: @matt_oncall

matt_oncall: acked. joining bridge now — will gather quick status.

sre-ashley: I can see the RoutePropagationDelay spike in CloudWatch, routes stuck in 'propagating' state for several attachments. ELB traffic to targets in AZC is seeing 502s/timeouts.

matt_oncall: running quick checks:
```bash
aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-route-tables --filters Name=transit-gateway-route-table-id,Values=tgw-rtb-0abc1234 --query 'Routes[*].{Dest:DestinationCidrBlock,State:State,Origin:Origin}' --output table
```

matt_oncall: output shows ~15 routes with State = "propagating" and Origin = "attachment/att-0f..." — that looks wrong.

eng-runtime: seeing 5xx surge and latency jump for svc-api-usw2c. Grafana spike matches the same window.

support-olivia: customers reporting timeouts and a few 502s; opened support ticket #12345 for affected accounts. Posting status page update in progress.

matt_oncall: quick mitigation options: 1) shift ELB traffic away from AZC by updating target-group weights 2) force route re-propagation by toggling the TGW attachment (detach/reattach) 3) request AWS control plane intervention. Thoughts?

sre-ashley: prefer option 1 immediately (less blast radius). I'll change target weights to 0 for AZC targets to route traffic to healthy AZs.

eng-runtime: confirm we can do a gradual shift — starting now.

<sre-ashley changed ELB target group weights: 2->0 for targets in AZC> :thumbsup:>

eng-runtime: error rate dropping from ~9% to ~2% after shifting traffic. latency also improving. Good.

matt_oncall: opened AWS case 987654321 (severity: impact to production) — asked for control-plane investigation into TGW propagation delays.

matt_oncall: if AWS can't resolve quickly we may need to detach and reattach the attachment to force repropagation. That will cause a short path change but should clear stuck routes. Planning that as option B.

jing: any customer-facing timeline?

support-olivia: status page updated: "Partial regional degradation in us-west-2c affecting routing/requests. Traffic being routed to other AZs. No data loss reported." Sending direct emails to customers with open tickets.

incident-bot: Reminder: on-call handoff scheduled in 30m. If incident remains active, please coordinate handoff.

matt_oncall: I'm going to keep monitoring and coordinate with AWS. Will not detach unless AWS recommends or error rates rise again. Leaving mitigation in place (traffic shifted).

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook hint: see runbook "tgw-route-propagation" — steps for verifying tgw routes and safe attachment reattach sequence: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/tgw-route-propagation

matt_oncall: logged immediate action items: (1) keep traffic shifted until propagation stable (2) await AWS response on case 987654321 (3) plan automated traffic-shift playbook for future (4) post-incident RCA and update runbook.

jing: hypothesis for RCA: transient AWS control-plane throttle in us-west-2c causing delayed route table propagation; need datasources: CloudWatch TGW metrics, AWS case logs, ELB target health history.

support-olivia: customer comms: will follow-up when AWS case updated and when we have RCA.

sre-ashley: creating a short incident summary for ops channel and will start draft of RCA. ETA first draft in 24h.

matt_oncall: handing to next oncall in 25m — @sre-ashley will take lead if I'm unavailable. Leaving notes in the incident doc.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial (traffic shifted); monitoring. Next update in 30 mins or on AWS case update. :white_check_mark:
